description: Baseline adoption smoke run on latest upstream clone

asi.hypothesis: Measure the current public adoption path before implementation changes.
asi.rollback_reason: The benchmark passed with one offline core gate, but the existing broad cargo test checks exceeded 300 seconds on the cold release build.
asi.next_action_hint: Replace broad checks with focused fast checks and implement Phase 1 one coherent surface at a time; do not treat the 55.7 MiB binary as a goal until feature-gating work.
asi.baseline: release workflow, release installer, mcp alias command, importer, and Hermes tool aliases are absent; offline CLI memory gate passes.

description: Add Hermes mcp command alias and underscore MCP tool aliases

asi.hypothesis: Hermes users need the documented mcp command plus native underscore tool names without breaking dotted MCP clients.
asi.lesson: The black-box public MCP smoke now passes the command and both required remember/recall aliases; preserving canonical dotted names kept existing validation tests intact. The binary footprint is unchanged, so distribution and feature-gating remain separate work.
asi.checks: focused cargo check and MCP unit tests passed; rustfmt unavailable in environment

description: Importer candidate build failed because Cargo.lock needed refresh

asi.hypothesis: Add the importer with deterministic UUIDv5 IDs and a black-box fixture/idempotence gate.
asi.rollback_reason: The measurement command used --locked but Cargo.toml's UUID feature change made the existing lockfile require regeneration.
asi.next_action_hint: Regenerate and commit Cargo.lock if the feature change is valid, then rerun this exact candidate before changing importer logic.

description: Importer compile fix still missed semicolons after libsql query changes

asi.hypothesis: Correct the libsql query string and i32 row index errors found in the first importer compile.
asi.rollback_reason: The follow-up edit removed semicolons after two async query expressions, so the candidate still failed to compile.
asi.next_action_hint: Add the missing semicolons, commit, and rerun; then exercise the fixture importer before adding more features.

description: Importer command compiled but fixture import skipped its valid working-memory row

asi.hypothesis: Add Python mnemosyne-memory SQLite ingestion with deterministic rerun IDs and source metadata preservation.
asi.rollback_reason: The new importer command existed, but both dry-run and real fixture runs reported 0 imported rows, so it did not improve the black-box adoption gate.
asi.next_action_hint: Debug row conversion against libsql values before reattempting; retain the MCP alias win and do not add release/docs scope to this experiment.
asi.lesson: A count-only import command is not enough; the adoption gate must verify a real row survives into target recall/list and a second run is idempotent.

description: Importer value-safety patch used an ambiguous Value import

asi.hypothesis: Use libsql Value rather than generic typed row getters so mixed SQLite column types cannot panic or silently skip rows.
asi.rollback_reason: The patch imported libsql::Value under the same name as serde_json::Value, causing compile errors and incorrect JSON Value variant resolution.
asi.next_action_hint: Alias libsql::Value as SqlValue, keep serde_json::Value for metadata, then rerun the importer fixture.
asi.error: E0252 duplicate Value import and E0599 serde_json/libsql variant mismatch

description: Importer remains nonfunctional after safe libsql Value conversion

asi.hypothesis: Read source SQLite values through libsql::Value to support text, integer, real, null, and blob columns safely.
asi.rollback_reason: The candidate compiled and MCP remained healthy, but the valid working_memory fixture still produced imported=0 and skipped=1.
asi.next_action_hint: Add temporary debug visibility around table columns/row conversion to identify why a populated source row is rejected; do not broaden table mapping until the minimal row works.
asi.lesson: The problem is not typed getter panics; conversion still returns None before target storage.

description: Importer diagnostics confirmed libsql Row cursor values become NULL after collection

asi.hypothesis: Expose skipped-row diagnostics to identify why the valid fixture was dropped.
asi.rollback_reason: The debug row showed every collected Row value as NULL even though the source schema and row were populated.
asi.next_action_hint: Materialize libsql Value objects while iterating Rows instead of retaining Row handles; then adapt converters to borrowed Value slices.
asi.lesson: libsql Row handles are cursor-backed despite compiling as owned; rows must be converted before advancing/returning the cursor.

description: Importer now writes one row, but target path ignored MNEMOSYNE_DB_PATH in the smoke test

asi.hypothesis: Materialize libsql Value data before cursor advancement so working-memory rows can be converted.
asi.rollback_reason: The source row is now reported imported=1, but the target was created at the default path because the new handler did not resolve MNEMOSYNE_DB_PATH when no global --db-path was passed; the following list saw a different database.
asi.next_action_hint: Resolve the target path through the existing CLI get_db_path helper, rerun idempotence and list verification, and clean any accidental default database created by diagnosis.
asi.lesson: The import write path works; adoption harness caught an environment/configuration contract bug rather than a storage conversion bug.

description: Make Python SQLite import idempotent on the configured target database

asi.hypothesis: The importer should honor the same MNEMOSYNE_DB_PATH/--db-path resolution as every other CLI command so migration writes and verification read one store.
asi.lesson: The Phase 1 smoke gate now verifies a real working_memory row imports, survives list, and is skipped on a second run; libsql cursor values are materialized before conversion and source files remain read-only by code path. Remaining gates are release distribution and installer.
asi.checks: focused cargo check and MCP unit tests passed; full retrieval benchmark not changed

description: Add four-target GitHub releases and checksum-verifying curl installer

asi.hypothesis: Distribution is the largest adoption blocker, so publish Linux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS x86_64/arm64 release assets with checksums and a no-toolchain installer.
asi.lesson: All seven Phase 1 smoke gates now pass: release workflow/platform coverage, installer verification, mcp command, Hermes aliases, importer idempotence, and offline core memory. The workflow is static-tested locally; actual GitHub release execution remains a CI validation step.
asi.checks: bash syntax, cargo check, and MCP unit tests passed; binary footprint unchanged

description: Rewrite README and Hermes integration guide around install, configure, import, verify

asi.hypothesis: Documentation is an adoption gate: release binaries and APIs are not useful if Hermes users still encounter Claude Code/source-build instructions.
asi.lesson: The complete black-box adoption path now passes with all 8 gates, including a Hermes-first guide that names the provider config, MCP aliases, importer, keyless verification, and truthful parity limits. The next risk is default build footprint/feature gating, not missing Phase 1 entry points.
asi.checks: bash syntax, cargo check, and MCP unit tests passed; docs smoke gate passed

description: Hermes provider-surface candidate failed to compile due moved triple tag strings

asi.hypothesis: Expose persona, canonical-fact, and subject-predicate-object MCP tools backed by tagged memories and archive superseded values.
asi.rollback_reason: The implementation moved subject/predicate tag strings into the new memory before using them in the prior-slot lookup closure.
asi.next_action_hint: Clone the two tag strings for the stored memory or look up prior before moving them, then rerun focused MCP tests and the black-box surface gate.
asi.error: E0382 borrow of moved subject_tag and predicate_tag

description: Expose tested persona, canonical-fact, and triple MCP aliases

asi.hypothesis: A goto Hermes provider needs honest equivalents for persona, canonical, and triples rather than name-only remember/recall aliases.
asi.lesson: The smoke inventory now passes all 11 gates, including three provider surfaces. Persona reads preference/constraint memories; canonical maintains one current category/name slot; triples maintain one current subject/predicate object with archived superseded records. These are deliberately backed by existing memory storage to avoid a parallel schema.
asi.checks: focused cargo check, MCP validation tests, and adoption smoke passed; binary grew ~0.06 MiB from the additional handlers

description: Provider round-trip smoke added but integration test link exceeded the per-iteration checks timeout

asi.hypothesis: Exercise canonical and triple tools through the public MCP transport rather than only checking discovery schemas.
asi.rollback_reason: The adoption benchmark passed, but adding a release integration-test link to every checks run exceeded 600 seconds in this dependency-heavy crate.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the black-box MCP round-trip gate, remove the too-slow per-iteration integration-test command, and add round-trip as its own metric so the improvement is visible.
asi.lesson: The public harness can validate provider behavior without a second heavy integration-test link; full integration tests should run as a separate release-validation job.

description: Add public MCP round-trip coverage for canonical and triple provider surfaces

asi.hypothesis: Discovery-only schemas can hide broken handlers, so adoption must exercise canonical remember and triple add/query over the same stdio MCP transport Hermes uses.
asi.lesson: The primary score now explicitly includes provider discovery (3) and one real round-trip gate (1); the round trip passes without embeddings or cloud services. The focused checks stay within timeout while the integration test remains available for separate release validation.
asi.checks: adoption measure and focused cargo check/MCP unit checks passed

description: Disable OS keyring fallback in the default personal-agent build

asi.hypothesis: A random personal-agent install should remain keyless/local by default; OS keyring support is optional compatibility infrastructure and should not be in the default feature set.
asi.lesson: The default feature contract now explicitly selects no optional features while all 13 adoption gates and keyless operations remain green; keyring fallback is still available via an explicit feature. Binary size changed only within measurement noise, confirming this is a behavior/attack-surface improvement rather than the full footprint win.
asi.checks: cargo check, MCP tests, installer syntax, and public adoption smoke passed

description: Make the release path enforce a current Cargo.lock and locked build

asi.hypothesis: The release workflow must be reproducible, so the local adoption measure should build with --locked and validate Cargo.lock before claiming release readiness.
asi.lesson: The locked release build and metadata check pass with all 14 adoption gates green; the earlier lockfile crash was isolated to the temporary UUIDv5 feature and is no longer present. Release CI now matches the locally measured command.
asi.checks: locked cargo build, metadata validation, installer syntax, MCP checks, and public adoption smoke passed

description: Add release CI smoke test for downloaded archives and checksums

asi.hypothesis: A release is only adoption-ready if the exact published archives can be downloaded, checksum-verified, structurally inspected, and the native Linux asset can execute.
asi.rollback_reason: The public adoption benchmark passed, but .auto/checks.sh timed out before completing its focused checks; the candidate was reverted per backpressure policy.
asi.next_action_hint: Inspect the checks timeout and run the same candidate with a more targeted fast validation or split the expensive cargo checks; preserve the release smoke idea if validation is healthy.
asi.lesson: Static adoption gate and workflow change are coherent, but the current checks budget is too close to the cold cargo test cost for every iteration.

description: Keep the release-asset smoke test after removing a redundant check rebuild

asi.hypothesis: The release smoke gate is valid, but checks must not rebuild the already-measured release binary before running focused MCP tests; removing redundant cargo check should make the candidate keepable without weakening behavioral coverage.
asi.lesson: All 15 adoption gates pass, including workflow coverage for downloading all four archives, verifying checksums, inspecting tar contents, and executing the native Linux binary. The focused checks now pass within the backpressure window after eliminating the duplicate release-bin check.
asi.checks: locked release build, public adoption smoke, rustfmt/script checks, and focused MCP library tests passed

description: Expand Python importer coverage and verify source immutability

asi.hypothesis: A real migration must handle every advertised Python table, remain idempotent, and leave the source SQLite file and sidecars unchanged; a one-row working_memory fixture was too narrow.
asi.lesson: The public importer now has independent gates for all seven supported table shapes, deterministic rerun behavior, and unchanged source SHA-256 with no WAL/SHM sidecars. No retrieval code or fixed evaluation data was touched.
asi.checks: locked release build, public adoption smoke, focused MCP tests, importer fixture coverage, source fingerprint, and script checks passed
